Generate polyplug plugin boilerplate

Usage: polyplugc <COMMAND>

Commands:
  generate  Generate code from an api.toml or bundle.toml
  validate  Validate an api.toml / bundle.toml, or an assembled bundle directory
  keygen    Generate an Ed25519 keypair for bundle signing
  sign      Sign a bundle directory, writing a `bundle.sig` file
  verify    Verify a bundle directory's `bundle.sig`
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

result.stdout:
Generate code from an api.toml or bundle.toml

Usage: polyplugc generate [OPTIONS] --lang <LANG> --out <OUT>

Options:
      --api <API>        Path to api.toml (generates host-side code)
      --bundle <BUNDLE>  Path to bundle.toml (generates guest-side code)
  -l, --lang <LANG>      Target language: rust, cpp, csharp, python, lua, js-quickjs
  -o, --out <OUT>        Output directory for generated files
  -h, --help             Print help

result.stdout:
Generate an Ed25519 keypair for bundle signing.

Writes two files into `--out`: - `signing.key`   (private — keep secret, 0o600) - `verifying.key` (public  — distribute alongside bundles or embed)

Usage: polyplugc keygen --out <OUT>

Options:
  -o, --out <OUT>
          Directory to write the keypair files into

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

result.stdout:
Sign a bundle directory, writing a `bundle.sig` file.

Runs the same validation checks as `validate --bundle-dir` first, then computes the canonical bundle digest and writes a detached signature.

Usage: polyplugc sign --bundle-dir <BUNDLE_DIR> --key <KEY>

Options:
      --bundle-dir <BUNDLE_DIR>
          Path to the assembled bundle directory

      --key <KEY>
          Path to the signing key file produced by `keygen`

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
